translationRepairs: When Cong took charge of the Directorate of Revenue, Yan was recommended as an inspection officer. He followed Cong again to Huainan and later entered the capital as a remonstrating censor.
When Cong took charge of the Directorate of Revenue, Yan was recommended as an inspection officer. He followed Cong again to Huainan and later entered the capital as an attending censor.
入拜侍御史 is appointment as attendant/serving censor; 諫官 or 諫議大夫 would be the remonstrating office.
When Cong headed the revenue bureau, Yan was listed as an inspection officer. He again followed Cong to Huainan, then entered court as remonstrating censor.
When Cong headed the revenue bureau, Yan was listed as an inspection officer. He again followed Cong to Huainan, then entered court as attending censor.
The same 侍御史 is mistranslated as remonstrating censor in the literal line.

When the chief minister learned of this, he appointed Yan Director of Military Appointments while also making him a remonstrating censor in charge of miscellaneous matters, and then summoned him into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

When the chief minister learned of this, he appointed Yan Director of Military Appointments while also making him an attending censor in charge of miscellaneous matters, and then summoned him into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.
兼侍御史知雜事 is an attending censor handling Censorate miscellaneous business, not a remonstrating censor.

When the Tangut troubled Hexi, Emperor Xuanzong once summoned him to inquire about border affairs. Yan cited ancient and modern examples and laid out the situation for breaking the Qiang in great detail. The emperor said with pleasure: "I shall choose a capable commander—who says Pang and Mu are in my inner court? Will you go for me, sir?"

When the Tangut troubled Hexi, Emperor Xuanzong once summoned him to inquire about border affairs. Yan cited ancient and modern examples and laid out the situation for breaking the Qiang in great detail. The emperor said with pleasure: "I shall choose a capable commander—who would have thought that Po and Mu were right here in my inner court? Will you go for me, sir?"
孰謂 marks surprise that 頗 and 牧 are already in the inner court; 頗 is Po, not Pang, and the original reads as a denial.
Soon afterward he again held the title of co-director while serving as military commissioner of Hedongzhong.
Soon afterward he again held the title of co-director while serving as military commissioner of Hezhong.
節度河中 is Hezhong; Hedongzhong conflates 河中 with 河東.
Soon he also served as co-director while commissioner of Hedongzhong.
Soon he also served as co-director while commissioner of Hezhong.
The literal line likewise misreads 河中 as Hedongzhong.

The chief minister took note and appointed him Director of Military Appointments while also serving as remonstrating censor handling miscellaneous matters, then summoned him into the Hanlin Academy as academician.

The chief minister took note and appointed him Director of Military Appointments while also serving as attending censor handling miscellaneous matters, then summoned him into the Hanlin Academy as academician.
侍御史知雜事 is attending censor for miscellaneous Censorate matters, not a remonstrating censor.

When the Tangut were raiding along the Hexi frontier, Emperor Xuanzong once summoned Yan to consult him on border affairs. Yan drew on ancient and modern precedents and set out a detailed plan for defeating the Qiang. Delighted, the emperor said, "I mean to choose a capable commander—who would have thought that Pang and Mu were right here in my inner court? Will you go on my behalf, sir?"

When the Tangut were raiding along the Hexi frontier, Emperor Xuanzong once summoned Yan to consult him on border affairs. Yan drew on ancient and modern precedents and set out a detailed plan for defeating the Qiang. Delighted, the emperor said, "I mean to choose a capable commander—who would have thought that Po and Mu were right here in my inner court? Will you go on my behalf, sir?"
頗 in the paired allusion 頗、牧 is Po (Lian Po); Pang is a mistranscription.
He was related to Wang Ning as a cousin by marriage.
He was a maternal cousin of Wang Ning.
外昆弟 is maternal-side cousinhood, not kinship by marriage.

When Ning's mother heard that Yanhao had become chancellor, she ordered the maids to make many pairs of shoes and socks, saying, "Wang's sister-in-law will surely be driven out together with her son. I shall go into exile with them."

When Ning's mother heard that Yanhao had become chancellor, she ordered the maids to make many pairs of shoes and socks, saying, "Wang's sister will surely be driven out together with her son. I shall go into exile with them."
王氏妹 is a Wang sister; sister-in-law would require 嫂, 婦, or similar affinal terms.
Ye was orphaned while still young. His mother was disabled by illness, and Sanfu begged for grain to support her.
Sanfu was orphaned while still young. His mother was disabled by illness, and he begged for grain to support her.
After 父三復, 少孤 and 三復丐粟 describe Sanfu’s youth, not Liu Ye.
Ye lost his father young; his mother was crippled by illness, and Sanfu begged grain to support her.
Sanfu lost his father young; his mother was crippled by illness, and Sanfu begged grain to support her.
The literal line repeats the same wrong subject for 少孤.
In the Huichang era when he reached chancellor he promoted Sanfu to Vice Minister of Punishments and Hanlin academician.
In the Huichang era when he reached chancellor he promoted Sanfu to Vice Minister of Punishments and scholar of the Hongwen Academy.
弘文館學士 is a scholar of the Hongwen Academy, not a Hanlin academician.
When Yizong succeeded and left office, Ye then petitioned to rectify his wrong and restored office and titles; the age highly honored this righteousness.
When Yizong succeeded and Linghu left office, Ye then petitioned to rectify Deyu's wrong and restored office and titles; the age highly honored this righteousness.
去位 continues 令狐久當國: Linghu left office. 其冤 is Deyu’s wrongful condemnation, not Yizong’s abdication.
Later Yang Shou, Wei Baoheng, Lu Yan, Lu She, Liu Ye, Yu Cong, Li Tan, and Cui Hang—none of them came to a peaceful end, just as he had foretold.
Later Yang Shou, Wei Baoheng, Lu Yan, Lu She, Liu Ye, Yu Cong, Doulu Zuan, and Cui Hang—none of them came to a peaceful end, just as he had foretold.
彖與沆 abbreviates Doulu Zuan and Cui Hang, not a separate Li Tan. Bare “Zuan” is still incomplete beside the surrounding full names.
Later Yang Shou, Wei Baoheng, Lu Yan, Lu She, Liu Ye, Yu Cong, Li Tan, and Cui Hang—all did not end well, as he said.
Later Yang Shou, Wei Baoheng, Lu Yan, Lu She, Liu Ye, Yu Cong, Doulu Zuan, and Cui Hang—all did not end well, as he said.
彖 is Doulu Zuan, not Li Tan; the literal list should restore the full name in parallel with Cui Hang.

When the emperor read his composition, he sighed and said, "In the Zhenyuan era Lu Zan and the Wu brothers, Tongxuan and Tongming, were masters of inner-court documents. After them there was no successor—until now, when I have found one in you."

When the emperor read his composition, he sighed and said, "In the Zhenyuan era Lu Zan and Wu Tongxuan and his brother were masters of inner-court documents. After them there was no successor—until now, when I have found one in you."
吳通玄兄弟 names Tongxuan and an unnamed brother; Tongming is invented, but “Tongxuan and his brother” is redundant after “Wu brothers.”
He rose through repeated promotions to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiaxing.
He rose through repeated promotions to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiaxing.
尚書左丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.
He rose repeatedly to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiaxing.
He rose repeatedly to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiaxing.
The literal line repeats the same misidentification of 尚書左丞 as a Secretariat post.

When the Prince of Siyu raised an army to attack Fengxiang, Yi remonstrated, saying, "The fortunes of the state have only just begun to settle. It is not fitting to bring additional troops so close to the capital. Other marauders will surely take advantage of the situation, and nothing will be gained.

When the succeeding Prince of Tan raised an army to attack Fengxiang, Yi remonstrated, saying, "The fortunes of the state have only just begun to settle. It is not fitting to bring additional troops so close to the capital. Other marauders will surely take advantage of the situation, and nothing will be gained.
嗣覃王 is the succeeding Prince of Tan; Siyu treats 嗣覃 as a toponym.

When the Siyu King raised troops to attack Fengxiang, Yi remonstrated: "The nation's fortune is just settling; it is not fitting to add troops near the capital—other bandits will surely take advantage, to no benefit.

When the succeeding Prince of Tan raised troops to attack Fengxiang, Yi remonstrated: "The nation's fortune is just settling; it is not fitting to add troops near the capital—other bandits will surely take advantage, to no benefit.
The literal “Siyu King” is the same misreading of 嗣覃王.
After passing the jinshi examination, he served as a remonstrating censor and rose step by step to Director of the Left Secretariat.
After passing the jinshi examination, he served as an investigating censor and rose step by step to Director of the Left Bureau.
監察御史 is the investigating censor, not a remonstrating censor, but 左司郎中 is still misread as a Secretariat post.
After passing the jinshi examination he served as remonstrating censor and rose through Left Secretariat Director.
After passing the jinshi examination he served as investigating censor and rose through Director of the Left Bureau.
The literal line needs both 監察御史 as investigating censor and 左司郎中 as Left Bureau director, not Left Secretariat.
When his term ended he left, having earned a thousand strings of cash stored in the prefectural treasury.
When his term ended he left, with a surplus of a thousand strings of cash stored in the prefectural treasury.
贏錢千緡藏州庫 is surplus cash left in the treasury, not money he had earned.
When Wang Hui served as censor-in-chief, he appointed Qi Military Department director in charge of miscellaneous matters, and Qi was later promoted to drafting attendant.
When Wang Hui served as censor-in-chief, he nominated Qi, a Military Department director, to take charge of miscellaneous matters, and Qi was later promoted to drafting attendant.
以兵部郎中表知雜事 is Wang Hui’s nomination of Zheng Qi, already a War Bureau director, to miscellaneous Censorate duty; 表 is not a simple appointment to a fused post.
After the Datun era, royal administration grew weak. Qi often used songs and ballads to offer veiled criticism, and palace eunuchs would recite them before the emperor.
After the Dashun era, royal administration grew weak. Qi often used songs and ballads to offer veiled criticism, and palace eunuchs would recite them before the emperor.
大順 is the Dashun era; Datun misreads 順.
After Datun royal administration grew weak; Qi often used songs and ballads with indirect satire; palace insiders who recited them before the Son of Heaven.
After Dashun royal administration grew weak; Qi often used songs and ballads with indirect satire; palace insiders who recited them before the Son of Heaven.
The literal line repeats Datun for 大順.

West of Xiang and Deng several hundred li of Yi warmth; east the Han chariot and Fenglin as its passes; south Jutan bends and flows into the Han; west the dangerous heights of Shangluo mountains; north Bais precipice linked—terrain advantageous, fertile fields.

West of Xiang and Deng several hundred li of level, warm land; east, Han Yu and Fenglin form its passes; south, Jutan bends and flows into the Han; west the dangerous heights of Shangluo mountains; north, white cliffs link together—advantageous terrain and fertile fields.
漢輿 and 白崖 are a place-name and white cliffs, not “Han chariot” or “Bais,” but “frontier” is not in 夷溫.

Wo placed second in the jinshi examination and rose through eminent offices. He became Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while serving as Vice Minister of Revenue, was transferred to the Chancellery, and was appointed overall commander of the four-sided campaign against Fengxiang.

Wo passed the jinshi examination and rose through eminent offices. He became Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while serving as Vice Minister of Revenue, was transferred to the Chancellery, and was appointed overall commander of the four-sided campaign against Fengxiang.
第進士 is obtaining the jinshi degree; 第 is not a rank of second.
Wo second in jinshi, passed through eminent offices; as Revenue Vice Minister Co-Director; moved to Chancellery; made overall commander of Fengxiang four-sided campaign.
Wo obtained the jinshi degree, passed through eminent offices; as Revenue Vice Minister Co-Director; moved to Chancellery; made overall commander of Fengxiang four-sided campaign.
The literal “second in jinshi” is the same misreading of 第進士.
He passed the jinshi examination and served on the staff of the Hedong command.
He passed the jinshi examination and served on the staff of the Hezhong command.
佐河中幕府 is the Hezhong command, not Hedong (河東).
He passed the jinshi examination and aided the Hedong staff.
He passed the jinshi examination and aided the Hezhong staff.
The literal line repeats Hedong for 河中.

In the year after Wo's demotion the emperor gave a feast at the Wensi ball ground. When Quanzhong entered, the officials were all seated beneath the corridor, and Quanzhong grew angry. He demoted Yi to militia vice-prefect of Di Prefecture and the remonstrating attendant Gui Ai to registrar of Deng Prefecture.

In the year after Wo's demotion the emperor gave a feast at the Wensi ball ground. When Quanzhong entered, the officials were all seated beneath the corridor, and Quanzhong grew angry. He demoted Yi to militia vice-prefect of Di Prefecture and the attendant censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou.
侍御史 is attendant censor, and 登州 is Dengzhou, not 鄧州 Deng Prefecture.

The year after Wo's demotion the emperor feasted at the Wensi ball ground; Quanzhong entered; the hundred officials sat beneath the corridor; Quanzhong was angry and demoted Yi to Militia Vice-Prefect of Di and Remonstrating Attendant Gui Ai to Registrar of Deng.

The year after Wo's demotion the emperor feasted at the Wensi ball ground; Quanzhong entered; the hundred officials sat beneath the corridor; Quanzhong was angry and demoted Yi to Militia Vice-Prefect of Di and Attendant Censor Gui Ai to Registrar of Dengzhou.
The literal line likewise renders 侍御史 as remonstrating attendant and 登州 as Deng.
